initial_observation.demographics: A 61-year-old Syrian male with a history of alcoholism and heavy smoking
initial_observation.chief_complaint: itchy pigmented lesions without telangiectasias, scaling, or atrophy on the right side of his trunk and his right thigh
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient had persistent hyperpigmented itchy patches for 3 years on the right trunk and right thigh, without other clinical features. Blood tests were normal except for a slight elevation in white blood cell count. No history of chemical exposure or family history of skin diseases.
presenting_symptoms: persistent hyperpigmented patches on right side of trunk and right thigh
known_prior_history: no prior exposure to chemicals or solvents
no family history of skin cancers or diseases

evidence_items.source_text: Upon clinical examination, hyperpigmented patches on the right side of his trunk and the lateral surface of his right thigh were evident, with no other clinical features (Fig. 1).
Blood tests of the patient were all within normal ranges except a slight increase in the white blood cell count.

histopathological examination of the biopsy revealed parakeratosic hyperkeratosic epidermis with slight spongiosis. Papillary dermis was infiltrated moderately by atypical lymphocytes with mild deposition of melanophages. Lymphocytic infiltrate was situated in clusters and in linear basilar distribution along the dermoepidermal junction (Fig. 2).
Immunochemistry of the atypical lymphocytes were CD3+, CD8+, CD4−, CD20−.
A chest and abdomen computed tomography (CT) scan was conducted, but yielded only normal findings with no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.
The patient was diagnosed with early stage HPMF and was subsequently referred to a specialized hospital to receive the treatment.

Our patient underwent psoralen and ultraviolet A light (PUVA) therapy, with oral 8-methoxypsoralen two times a week, and was prescribed a topical 0.1% betamethasone dipropionate. After 12 weeks of treatment, the itching was relieved, and the hyperpigmentation regressed, but did not disappear.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: The patient was diagnosed with early stage HPMF
